content: When your immune system becomes stronger, it may start to combat infections you have previously experienced. This can potentially lead to the reappearance of disease symptoms. Additionally, if your immune system becomes overactive, you may also experience symptoms. This immune response can occur at any time, either shortly after initiating HIV treatment or even months later. Severe allergic reactions to this medication are rare. However, this is not an exhaustive list of potential side effects. If you are in the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice regarding side effects. Similarly, if you are in Canada, consult your doctor for guidance on side effects. Precautions: Before starting cobicistat, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could trigger allergic reactions or other complications. This medication is not recommended for use during pregnancy, as it may not be effective in pregnant women. If you become pregnant or suspect you might be pregnant, notify your doctor immediately. It is currently unknown whether this medication passes into breast milk. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions can alter the effectiveness of your medications or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs as well as herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Cobicistat can slow the elimination of other medications from your body, potentially affecting how they work. Conversely, other medications can influence the removal of cobicistat from your body, which may impact its effectiveness. Examples of such medications include certain drugs used to treat seizures (e.g., carbamazepine, phenobarbital, phenytoin, primidone), enzalutamide, specific HIV NNRTI drugs (e.g., efavirenz, etravirine, nevirapine), mitotane, and rifampin. This medication may reduce the effectiveness of hormonal birth control methods such as pills, patches, or rings, potentially leading to pregnancy. Discuss with your doctor or pharmacist whether you should use reliable backup birth control methods while taking this medication. Overdose: In the event of an overdose with serious symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Lab Tests: Laboratory and/or medical tests (e.g., kidney function tests) may be conducted before you start this medication and periodically while you are taking it. Ensure you attend all medical and laboratory appointments. Missed Dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is less than 12 hours before your next dose, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Storage: Store this medication in its original container at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Important Information: This document provides a summary and does not contain all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individualized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
